label: input token q during the original phase (position >= 2)
explanation: A token detector for q. It fires only when q is input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, and every activation is on a q input. It never fires on q at positions 0 or 1, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase, including when q is fed back as an input or is the token being output. Magnitude depends on position: activations are weak at t=2 and at the last positions (t=7-8, where firing is rare), and strongest for q at t=3-6, where about 33% of q inputs fire. A repeated q fires more weakly the first time and more strongly the second (e.g. m n r [q:0.58] [q:0.96]). All twelve top-activating examples begin with m, but I did not test whether that is a real effect. The false positives are q inputs, mostly at t=2 or t=8, where the feature stays silent.

issues: The core finding holds. On dev, 100% of activations are on q inputs in the original phase at t>=2. Nothing fires at t=0-1, on <DEL>, or in the copy phase (phase table: delimiter 0, copy 0). Misses on the test split show 0 missed activations.

One factual claim is wrong: 'about 33% of q inputs fire at t=3-6'. That 0.033 is the firing rate over all steps at that orig_idx, not over q inputs. Over q inputs, precision is 0.990 at t=3, 0.997 at t=4, 0.985 at t=5 and 0.911 at t=6.

The false positives follow a position pattern, not scattered noise. The q firing rate is 0.55 at t=2, 0.52 at t=7 and 0.076 at t=8. 'Position >= 2' overclaims: at t=8 the feature almost never fires (P=0.076, mass recall 0.001), and t=2 fires only about half the time with low magnitude (mass recall 0.042 vs recall 0.152).
Partial structure at t=2: a q after a digit fires 80% of the time (P=0.801), against about 52% after a letter. This is a secondary history effect that the explanation does not mention.

The claim that 'a repeated q fires more weakly the first time and more strongly the second' cannot be right as a general rule. The first occurrence comes earlier, so its activation cannot depend on the later q. The top examples (q at t=3 at 0.58, then q at t=4 at 0.96) fit an ordinary position or context difference. Over all q inputs, firing rates for first vs repeat occurrences are similar (P 0.819 vs 0.781).

The first-token-m effect is small. q with first_tok==m has P=0.849 vs 0.813, and a mass/recall ratio of about 1.4, so magnitude is somewhat higher. It explains only 3.4% of activations, so it is minor.
Restricting to t<=7 is a modest, consistent gain: test F1 0.912 (P 0.842, R 0.996, mass recall 0.999) vs 0.897 for the original predicate.
